**The first day should produce a credible baseline and reveal what could invalidate it.** Define the actual decision, target, error costs, and success metric. Inspect timestamps, missingness, duplicates, label availability, and entity relationships before fitting a sophisticated model. [1](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/guides/rules-of-ml)

Create a deployment-appropriate temporal or grouped split. Compare a simple heuristic with a fast linear, tree, or pretrained baseline. By the end of the day, deliver reproducible code, held-out results, representative errors, and known limitations. A strong score without a trustworthy split is not a useful starting point.

**Use the next weeks to reduce the largest uncertainties.** First audit labels and failure patterns and version the data pipeline. Then improve the highest-value features or data and build serving checks, monitoring, load tests, and rollback. Finally shadow or canary the candidate and evaluate prespecified guardrails. [2](https://research.google/pubs/the-ml-test-score-a-rubric-for-ml-production-readiness-and-technical-debt-reduction/) [3](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/)

Three weeks is a planning target, not a universal production guarantee. Missing labels, integrations, or validation requirements may force a narrower release. Define supported cases and launch criteria so progress is reviewable. The goal is a reliable useful workflow with ownership and evidence, not merely a trained model file by a calendar date.

**Technical details and references.**

Day 1: define the business decision, target, costs, and success metric; inspect schema, missingness, duplicates, timestamps, and label availability. Create a leak-free temporal/entity split, then compare a dumb heuristic with a fast linear/GBDT or pretrained baseline. By 5 PM, deliver reproducible code, held-out metrics, representative errors, and known limitations. [1](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/guides/rules-of-ml)

Week 1: audit labels and worst errors, fix data/split issues, establish versioned datasets and a reproducible pipeline. Week 2: iterate on the highest-value data/features, build serving with input/schema checks, monitoring, load tests, and rollback. Week 3: shadow, canary, evaluate guardrails, document ownership, and expand only if criteria pass. [2](https://research.google/pubs/the-ml-test-score-a-rubric-for-ml-production-readiness-and-technical-debt-reduction/) [3](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/)

Three weeks is a planning target, not a universal promise: missing labels, integrations, validation requirements, or poor baseline quality can change scope. Agree on a narrow supported release and make unresolved risks visible through explicit launch criteria.
